title: Webhook signer + residency assertions + retention-enforcer API
creator: Sofia Kim
description: Build a focused API and webhook enhancer that achieves three goals: (1) sign outbound compliance webhooks with customer-scoped KMS keys and include a verifiable residency assertion object, (2) centralize retention enforcement via a "retention-enforcer" endpoint that can be polled or pushed to by downstream archival systems, and (3) provide a lightweight evidence-reporting batch export for auditors that includes signed lineage and TTL metadata.
background: Customers in regulated industries have requested stronger guarantees around where evidence is stored, how long audit data is retained, and immutable proof that retention actions (delete/retain/export) were taken. Current webhook delivery supports raw audit events but lacks: signed proofs, a canonical residency assertion schema, and a single control-plane API to reconcile retention state across regions and downstream archives.
acceptance_criteria: Outbound webhooks for compliance events include a JWS signature using customer KMS keys and a signature header; verification documented in developer guide.
Webhook payload contains a residency_assertion object (schema v1) with canonical fields: region, dataset_id, residency_guarantee, asserted_at, assertion_id.
Retention-enforcer API provides endpoints: POST /v1/retention/check, POST /v1/retention/apply, GET /v1/retention/status and returns canonical status (applied|pending|failed) with idempotency keys.
Signed export bundle generator creates NDJSON bundles with per-record signed metadata and an index manifest; manifest is signed by platform KMS and references customer signature roots.
Webhook retry and idempotency guarantees documented: at-least-once delivery with idempotent processing using event_id + signature verification.
End-to-end integration test that simulates cross-region residency change and verifies retention-enforcer rollback and signed audit evidence.
Performance: signing adds <10ms median per-webhook at p95 <25ms on our staging KMS cluster under 1000rps concurrent deliveries.
technical_notes: Signing: use AWS KMS asymmetric keys (ECDSA_SECG_P256K1 or ECDSA_P256) with JWS (compact) plus timestamp header.
Residency assertion: small canonical object to minimize webhook size; avoid including full PII — include dataset_id and a SHA256 hash of the evidence bundle for later verification.
Retention-enforcer: implement as control-plane idempotent commands; persist commands in retention ledger with event sourcing so that downstream reproducers can reconcile state.
Backfill: plan a migration job that emits signed 'residency-assertion' events for existing evidence; mark backfill window and rate-limit to avoid spiky load.
Retry: extend current webhook orchestrator to propagate original signature and assertion headers across retries to preserve verification semantics.
KMS tenancy: support customer-managed keys (CMKs) for enterprise tenants and a platform fallback key for hosted customers without CMKs. Key rotation recipe required.
Schema versioning: residency_assertion.v1 is the first stable contract; add header X-Residency-Assertion-Version for future compatibility.
Observability: surface per-webhook signature verification rates, KMS latency, and retention-enforcer command success/failure metrics in Console.
Rate-limiting: retention-enforcer apply commands require soft throttling for high-volume customers; add a token-bucket per-customer quota.
Security: threat model indicates possibility of replay attacks; include assertion_id + issued_at + signature which binds to event_id and TTL to mitigate replay.
Data residency change: when a customer moves region, emit a signed residency_migration event with pre- and post-region hashes to support audits.
decisions: Adopt JWS compact signatures with KMS-backed asymmetric keys for webhook signing (vs. raw HMAC) to support external verification without sharing secrets.
Keep residency_assertion small and schema-first to limit coupling with event payload changes.
Implement retention-enforcer as control-plane API with persistent ledger instead of a purely push model to simplify reconciliation and auditing.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Sofia Kim: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed on KMS-first approach; PM asked for export manifest to be signed by platform and include customer signature root.

2025-02-18 - Arjun Patel: Spiked KMS signing in staging; measured median 6ms, p95 18ms. Noted that AWS KMS cold-starts cause occasional 200ms outliers; will add a signing cache for high-throughput paths.

2025-02-22 - PM (Lena Ortiz): Added acceptance criteria to require idempotent retention commands and documented failure semantics; requested retention-enforcer also expose dry-run mode for safe audits.
2025-02-25 - Security (Maya Chen): Requested replay-protection details and threat-model update; flagged key-rotation with active signatures as important for compliance audits.

2025-02-28 - Arjun Patel: Implemented residency_assertion.v1 schema and added X-Residency-Assertion-Version header. Began wiring signed header into webhook orchestrator. Tests added for signature verification.

2025-03-01 - QA (Eli Roberts): Found intermittent failure when applying retention-enforcer commands for large customer (500k items) due to pagination bug; blocking root-cause investigation assigned to ENG-39503.
next_steps: Finish KMS signing cache and add circuit-breaker for KMS latency spikes.
Implement retention-enforcer API endpoints and ledger persistence with event-sourcing pattern.
Add dry-run mode to retention-enforcer and expose it to Console in a restricted preview.
Complete migration/backfill plan and run a small canary backfill for an internal test tenant.
Submit security review checklist and threat-model updates before GA.
